Let's have the story as the world believes it, Then have the truth. She was betrothed to him,
And so he mourned her, kept her face enshrined, Was wedded to her spirit, could not brook
This face of faces! So the story went Around the country. But his grief was not The grief they told. The pang that gnawed his heart,
Took root in shame, defeat, rejected love. He had gone east to meet her and to wed her,
He found his dear bride flown, a note for him, Left with the mother, saying she had flown,
She did not love him as a woman should Who makes a pact for life; her heart was set
To France for study, wished him well, in truth-- Some woman waited him who was his mate....
The letter, tried to find a secret hope Lodged back of words--was this a woman's way
He half resolved to follow her to France; Then as he thought of what he was himself
His egotism rose, fed by the hurt: She might stay on in France for aught he cared!
Such happiness and love? for he had given In a great passion out of a passionate heart
A gift like this? Yet always in his heart Stirred something which by him was love and hate.
She loved a maestro, and the word like gas, Which poisons, creeps and is not known, that death
Or broken love, disaster of some sort, His spirit withered with its bitterness.
With unreserve his heart, his leaves withheld From possible frost, dreamed on and drifted on
To seek and try, endure defeat again.
Of something yet to be to fill his hope Died not, but with each dawn awoke to move
The very cry of youth, which would not cease Kept all the dreams and passions of his youth
Rosy and agile as he neared the mark Of fifty years.
As one who waited. What would come to him? What soul would seek him in this room of books?

Thought Merival, of spirit, but what waste Of spirit in the lives he knew! What homes Where children starve for bread, or starve for love,
With aspirations broken, or with hopes Or talents bent or blasted! O, what wives

To ends that suit.
